## Intent

A 30-second product-launch showreel. The viewer should feel the craft and understand the product. Jon asked for a dynamic motion-graphics film, "like it's your showreel for a résumé," and said to go all out. Use https://agent-motion.com/ and real AuthHub interface, or both. - https://agent-motion.com/ — capture for component language, copy, and registry visuals.
- AuthHub product UI — real screens from the app, used as proof inside the reel.
- apps/web/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md — Acid Brutalism v2 is the brand. Coral is the accent. Ink and paper are the grounds.

## Customizations

- No voiceover. On-screen lines carry the script.
- Music bed. Cuts land on the beat. Sound hits on type slams.
- Before/after arc: the access chase, then one link, then the product working.
- Design system is chosen after capture and remixed onto AuthHub color and type. The pick is layout bones. The brand stays AuthHub.

- Length is 30 seconds, the top of the requested 15–30 second range, so the reel has room to move.
- Frame is 1920×1080. A résumé showreel is watched wide. The remembered LinkedIn 1080×1350 size was not used.
- Do not invent metrics, customer names, or platform claims the product does not make.
- One coral accent. Acid yellow is one hero moment only.

---
format: 1920x1080
duration: 30s
message: "One client link replaces the access chase"
arc: "BAB — the chase, then one link, then the product working"
audience: "Agency operators who chase client platform access, and people judging a motion reel"
mode: autonomous
music: "percussive kinetic electronic, tight drums, no vocals, tension then a clean resolve"
narration: no
captions: skipped (no spoken words; type is the picture)
---

## Video direction

Palette comes from `frame.md`. Canvas is `cream` (#FAFAFA) or `ink` (#09090B). The accent event is `yellow` (#FF6B35, AuthHub coral). `orange` (#CCFF00) is the single acid hit, and it appears once, on the claim. `pink` is a tint, not a second brand. Type roles: `display-hero` and `display-xl` for the words that are the shot, `mono-kicker` for labels, `body-md` only inside the product surface.

Motion grammar: long-tail settle (`power3`). No bounce, no overshoot, no breathing, no back-half camera drift. There is no spoken voiceover. On-screen lines are the cues. Each piece enters when its line arrives, across the back half of the shot, never dumped in the first quarter. Holds stay still. Subtle jitter is the only aliveness, and only on a resting hero. Internal swaps are velocity-matched cuts.

Rhythm: Frame 1 is the attack. Frame 2 is the held claim. Frame 3 is the product proof and the busiest shot. Frame 4 is a short status punch. Frame 5 holds the lockup still. Energy peaks at the coral slam and at the last letter of the wordmark.

Never: fake ROI numbers, invented customers, purple gradients, glassmorphism, pill-everything, lazy particle fields, infinite marquees, bouncy springs, or a screenshot of Agent Motion standing in for AuthHub. Bottom 17% stays clear of the hero.

## Frame 1 — The chase

- scene: Chase words roll in one slot, then ONE LINK shoves them off
- duration: 5.5s
- poster: 4.6s
- transition_in: cut
- status: outline
- type: hook
- persuasion: Open on the viewer's mess, not the product
- beat: tension
- blueprint: ticker-takeover (Adapt)
- focal: kinetic-type-swap
- asset_candidates: []
- roles: none — type is the subject
- sfx: tick, impact
- src: compositions/frames/01-chase.html
- handoff_out: element "ONE LINK"; x 960; y 470; scale 1; opacity 1; motion settled, still, centered

Adapt: keep the signature crash. The cycling slot is the chase. The hero that shoves it is the phrase ONE LINK, not a logo. Install and restyle `kinetic-type-swap` for the slot. The crash itself is the blueprint's off-screen shove, not a second component.

Scene 1 (0.0–1.1s): ink field. Mono kicker STILL CHASING sits upper third. Nothing else. Centered, sparse, two layers (field + kicker).
Scene 2 (1.1–3.2s): the fixed line "Send the" holds center-left. One masked slot rolls PASSWORD, then INVITE, then SCREENSHOT. Each swap is a vertical roll. The slot is the joke. Asymmetric, type occupies ~60% of the width. `kinetic-type-swap`.
Scene 3 (3.2–4.4s): ONE LINK enters from the right at speed and shoves the whole line off the left. The phrase lands heavy, coral (`yellow`) on ink, display-hero, dead center. The struck line is displaced. It does not fade.
Scene 4 (4.4–5.5s): ONE LINK holds still at center. Subtle jitter only. This pose is the handoff.

## Frame 2 — The claim

- scene: ONE LINK stays, the claim completes, AuthHub stamps once
- duration: 5s
- poster: 3.6s
- transition_in: cut
- status: outline
- type: product_intro
- persuasion: The promise lands before any feature
- beat: release
- blueprint: kinetic-type-beats (Adapt)
- focal: headline-slam
- asset_candidates: []
- roles: none — type is the subject
- sfx: impact
- src: compositions/frames/02-claim.html
- handoff_in: element "ONE LINK"; x 960; y 470; scale 1; opacity 1; motion settled, still, centered

Adapt: keep the in-place statement build and a hard-cut beat change. Do not bounce. `headline-slam` brings the second line in. Acid (`orange`) flashes once behind the word LINK, then dies. No second acid moment in the film.

Scene 1 (0.0–0.6s): the handoff pose only. ONE LINK, coral, centered on ink. No new element.
Scene 2 (0.6–2.4s): REPLACES THE ACCESS CHASE slams up under it in cream, display-lg, and settles on a long tail. ONE LINK shifts up to make room. The pair reads as one lockup, upper-middle, ~70% width.
Scene 3 (2.4–3.6s): a hard internal cut. The claim clears at peak speed. AUTHHUB lands in the same center, display-hero, cream on ink, with a 4px ink edge and a hard coral offset shadow. One acid block sits behind the word for this window only.
Scene 4 (3.6–5.0s): acid block is gone. AUTHHUB holds still. Mono kicker ONE CLIENT LINK sits beneath in coral. Stillness is the read.

## Frame 3 — The request

- scene: A real AuthHub request window completes the loop
- duration: 8s
- poster: 5.2s
- transition_in: cut
- status: outline
- type: feature_showcase
- persuasion: Show the loop, do not list features
- beat: proof
- blueprint: device-surface-showcase (Adapt)
- focal: browser-device-stage
- asset_candidates: []
- roles: none — the surface is built, not a captured screenshot
- sfx: whoosh, click
- src: compositions/frames/03-request.html

Adapt: keep the cursorless stepwise flow inside one held window. Drop the 3D hand and the bloom exit. Use `browser-device-stage` as the chrome. Screens are rebuilt from the live AuthHub request flow: Fundamentals, then Platforms, then a pending row. Copy stays faithful. Client fixture on screen is Acme Growth, the app's own sample, not a claimed customer result. Platforms named are ones the product actually connects: Google, Meta, Shopify, Klaviyo. No invented metrics.

Scene 1 (0.0–1.4s): cream field. Mono kicker NEW ACCESS REQUEST. The window is not on screen yet.
Scene 2 (1.4–3.2s): `browser-device-stage` slides in from the right and settles, centered, about half the frame tall, three layers (field, window, type). First screen: Step 1 of 4, FUNDAMENTALS active in coral, Select Client, the Acme Growth row. Camera static.
Scene 3 (3.2–5.2s): the step chrome stays. Content pushes left. PLATFORMS enters from the right. Four platform rows stagger in: Google, Meta, Shopify, Klaviyo. Each row is a bordered cell, not a logo collage.
Scene 4 (5.2–8.0s): content pushes again. A single request row holds: Acme Growth, a coral PENDING chip, the date 9/30/2026. Side line, mono, reads SENT. The window holds still. No end zoom.

## Frame 4 — The status

- scene: Four truthful dashboard counts land, then hold
- duration: 5.5s
- poster: 4.2s
- transition_in: cut
- status: outline
- type: benefit_highlight
- persuasion: Status you can see, not a productivity claim
- beat: proof
- blueprint: kinetic-type-beats (Adapt)
- focal: headline-slam
- asset_candidates: []
- roles: none
- sfx: tick
- src: compositions/frames/04-status.html

Adapt: the center-stage beats are four stat cells, not a sentence. Signature is the beat change: each cell arrives alone in rhythm, then they hold as a row. Numbers are the sample dashboard, not a market claim: 2 requests, 1 pending, 1 active connection, 2 platforms. Count-up is short and finishes before the hold. No percent, no "hours saved."

Scene 1 (0.0–1.0s): cream field. Mono kicker WHAT YOU SEE. Nothing else.
Scene 2 (1.0–3.6s): four cells arrive one at a time, left to right, each a hard-bordered square with an offset shadow. Labels in mono: TOTAL REQUESTS 2, PENDING 1, ACTIVE CONNECTIONS 1, PLATFORMS CONNECTED 2. Numbers use display scale and count up as each cell lands. The row sits on the upper-middle band, ~80% width.
Scene 3 (3.6–5.5s): the row holds still. A single cream line under it, display, reads NO MORE CHASING. No camera move.

## Frame 5 — Lockup

- scene: AuthHub wordmark builds and holds on the URL
- duration: 6s
- poster: 4.8s
- transition_in: cut
- status: outline
- type: cta
- persuasion: Leave the name and the place
- beat: resolve
- blueprint: logo-assemble-lockup (Adapt)
- focal: logo-brand-close
- asset_candidates: []
- roles: none — the wordmark is type, not the Agent Motion favicon
- sfx: impact
- src: compositions/frames/05-lockup.html

Adapt: keep the letter-by-letter build into a centered lockup, then a dead-still hold. Use `logo-brand-close`. Skip glow bloom and skip the Agent Motion mark. The accent period is a coral square, not a dot. URL is authhub.co. This is the only frame that may exit; it does not. It holds.

Scene 1 (0.0–2.2s): ink field. Letters of AUTHHUB cascade in from the left, display-hero, cream, and settle centered. The coral square lands last, hard offset shadow, no bounce.
Scene 2 (2.2–3.6s): mono line ONE CLIENT LINK fades up under the wordmark, tracked out, coral.
Scene 3 (3.6–6.0s): authhub.co settles beneath in cream mono. The lockup holds dead still through the last frame. No glow, no drift, no second slam.
